chapters.1.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches sound doctrine as protection against false instruction. Why does a teacher's conduct matter when whole households face disruption?
chapters.1.summary: The letter is addressed from Paul to Titus, his true child in faith. Paul left Titus in Crete to appoint elders in every city. An elder must be blameless, the husband of one wife, with believing children. An overseer must not be self-pleasing, quick to anger, violent, or greedy. He must be hospitable, self-controlled, and hold to the faithful word. Many unruly talkers upset whole households for dishonest gain. The letter quotes a Cretan saying against Cretans. Titus is to rebuke them sharply.
chapters.2.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches sound doctrine as protection against false instruction. How does grace supply the reason for good work within these unequal instructions?
chapters.2.summary: Titus is to teach what fits sound doctrine. Older men are to be sober and sound in faith. Older women are to teach the younger to love their husbands and children. Young men are to be self-controlled, and Titus is to be their example. Servants are to please their masters and not steal. The grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all. It trains people to live soberly while they wait for Christ’s appearing. He gave himself to redeem a people eager for good works.
chapters.3.lds: How do the closing travel requests make useful work concrete?
chapters.3.summary: Titus is to remind them to obey rulers and be gentle to all. The writers too were once foolish, disobedient, and hateful. Then God’s kindness appeared, and he saved them by mercy, not by their works. He did it through washing and renewal by the Holy Spirit. Those who believe should be careful to do good works. Titus should avoid foolish disputes and reject a divisive person after two warnings. Paul will send Artemas or Tychicus and asks Titus to come to Nicopolis. He should help Zenas and Apollos on their journey.
